alerts.after.desc: Boiler-on time, added up across runs.
alerts.none: No notify services found. Install the Home Assistant Companion app on a phone to get alerts there.
alerts.not_warming.desc: Alert when the boiler has been called this long without the house warming up.
alerts.sub: Tells you when the heating isn't working. Alerts always appear in Home Assistant's notifications too.
alerts.title: Alerts
app.subtitle: Intelligent Heating Control
app.title: Nook
energy.empty: No history yet — heat cycles will appear here.
energy.lead: When the boiler ran, setpoint changes, and Leaf days.
energy.title: Energy History
entities.title: Entities
error.entity_picker: Home Assistant entity picker is not available
helper.add_first: Add the panel first, then pair it with the Nook Panel Helper here.
helper.code_invalid: Enter the 6-digit code shown on the panel
helper.cpu_lock: Keep the panel running with the screen off
helper.cpu_lock.desc: A CPU wake lock. Off by default: on the NSPanel Pro a held lock stopped the screen turning off.
helper.hide.desc: Switches "Return to main program" off whenever Sonoff turns it back on
helper.hide.needs_permission: Needs its one-time permission — see the helper's screen.
helper.hide.not_found: Sonoff's button wasn't found on this panel.
helper.host.desc: Only if Nook can't find the panel — blank uses the linked Fully Kiosk device's address. Not the pairing code.
helper.intro: The Nook Panel Helper is a small app on the panel: it keeps Sonoff's floating "Return to main program" button hidden and tells Nook how the panel is doing. Open it on the panel and enter the code it shows.
helper.label: Helper:
helper.unpair.confirm: Unpair the helper? It keeps running on the panel; pair again with a new code.
helper.updates_tap: Updates: Need a tap on the panel
helper.wifi_lock: Keep Wi-Fi at full power with the screen off
helper.wifi_lock.desc: A Wi-Fi lock. Same caveat — try one at a time and check the screen still turns off.
hero.headline.trv_offline: TRV offline — changes apply when it's back
hero.hint.controlling: Controlling {name} — tap it again or Home to go back
hero.hint.reorder_touch: · drag to reorder (press and hold first)
hero.hint.tap_room: Tap a room to control its radiator
hero.no_rooms: No rooms yet — add TRVs on the Rooms tab.
hero.tile.tip_back: Click to go back to the house
intel.auto_schedule.desc: Learns schedule changes from your manual adjustments
intel.away_delay.desc: Switches to Eco once nobody's been home this long
intel.coast.desc: How much the leftover heat of the radiator "coasts" the room temperature
intel.leaf.desc: Rewards a leaf when you're saving energy
intel.sub: How Nook learns your habits and the environment to optimise your heating.
intel.title: Nook Intelligence
intel.true_radiant.desc: Learns how to hit your scheduled temperature perfectly without overheating.
intel.warmup.desc: How fast the house heats, used to time preheating
kiosk.auto_sync.desc: Re-applies these when a panel reconnects or drifts. The start URL is always set for you.
kiosk.drift.pin: Menu PIN differs from the wall PIN
kiosk.exit_gesture.1: Double-tap top left, then bottom right
kiosk.field.exit_gesture.desc: How Fully's menu and PIN dialog open while Kiosk Mode is on. Swipe from the left edge gets in the way of swiping to the wall panel's usage page. The PIN is the wall panel PIN (Settings).
kiosk.field.js_interface.desc: Lets the Nook wall app hear Fully's motion and screen-on events, so a wave clears the clock.
kiosk.field.kiosk_lock.desc: Stops anyone leaving the app on the panel. Needs Kiosk Mode turned on once at the panel; after that this switches it on and off from here.
kiosk.field.motion_detection.desc: Uses the panel's camera. Leave this off on panels without a camera, like the NSPanel Pro — Fully fails and restarts every few seconds.
kiosk.field.proximity_motion.desc: Uses the panel's proximity sensor — for panels without a camera, like the NSPanel Pro. Needs the JavaScript interface on.
kiosk.field.proximity_threshold.desc: Fully's proximity threshold. Its default is 50%.
kiosk.field.screen_brightness.desc: While the panel is in use.
kiosk.field.screen_off_timer.desc: Time since the last touch before the screen turns off (the clock shows first, after the panel's "Clock after"). Walking past then wakes it straight to the thermostat. 0 = never.
kiosk.field.screensaver_timer.desc: Fully's own screensaver. 0 = never — the Nook app already dims to its clock.
kiosk.field.stay_awake: Stay awake with the screen off
kiosk.field.stay_awake.desc: Keeps the panel and its Wi-Fi running while the screen is off, so it wakes straight to live data instead of reconnecting first. The screen still turns off.
kiosk.no_integration: Add the Fully Kiosk Browser integration in Home Assistant (needs Fully's Plus licence) to manage your panels from here.
kiosk.saved_sent.one: Saved — {count} change sent to your panels
kiosk.saved_sent.other: Saved — {count} changes sent to your panels
kiosk.sub: Fully Kiosk settings every panel shares. Leave a setting blank and Nook won't touch it.
kiosk.title: Kiosk Browser
leaf.foot: Earn a leaf by saving energy - turn down the heating, use Eco/Away, or switch the heating off.
leaf.sub_inactive: Turn the heat down, use Eco/Away, or switch off to earn Leaf time.
leaf.title: Leaf
overview.banner.not_warming: The house isn't warming up — the boiler has been called for {minutes} min and the house has only warmed {rise}°C. {cause} This clears once the house warms up again.
overview.banner.not_warming.boiler: Check the boiler is firing (power, pressure, fault code, call-for-heat wiring).
overview.banner.not_warming.closed: The TRVs that are online ({rooms}) have all closed their valves — their own sensor by the radiator reads the set temperature — so the heat isn't reaching the room the house sensor is in.
overview.banner.not_warming.offline.one: The {rooms} TRV is offline, so Nook can't open that radiator's valve.
overview.banner.not_warming.offline.othe: The {rooms} TRVs are offline, so Nook can't open those radiators' valves.
overview.banner.relay_unavailable: Boiler relay {relay} is unavailable — Nook cannot switch the boiler. Check the device, or pick another relay in Settings.
overview.banner.released: Boiler relay released for testing — Nook isn't switching it until {time} (or Take control in Settings).
preview.desc: {size} — the wall app bundled with this Nook version, live against your real entities, at the panel's screen shape. Saving a panel reloads it.
preview.missing: The wall app is missing from this Nook install — nothing at {url}.
preview.shield: View only — tick Allow taps to use it
preview.taps_live: Taps are live — they change the real heating
preview.title: Preview
relay.desc: Nook keeps the relay in step with the heating. Release it for up to an hour to test the relay by hand; Nook then takes it back automatically.
relay.release_confirm: Release the boiler relay for an hour? Nook stops switching it so you can test it by hand, then takes it back automatically.
relay.released.desc: Switch the relay by hand to test it. Nook takes control back at {time}.
reporting.queued: not sent yet — Nook sends it when Zigbee has settled and the sensor next reports
reporting.fast_recheck: reporting every 0.1°C / 5 min (set earlier — the sensor was asleep for today's re-check, Nook tries again)
room_dlg.calls.desc: Lets this room turn the boiler on when it's cold. Leave on for most TRVs — otherwise the valve can open with no hot water.
room_dlg.calibrate.desc: A TRV measures beside its hot radiator, so it reads high and shuts early. Nook keeps the TRV's own temperature offset matched to the room sensor above, so the TRV's screen shows the real room temperature and it closes at the right time. Needs a room temperature sensor.
room_dlg.extras.desc: Optional — averaged with the room sensor.
room_dlg.follow.desc: The room uses the house temperature (plus the offset below), so the house dial, schedule and presets move it too. Turn off to give the room its own temperatures.
room_dlg.hold_ends: A change made on this room lasts until
room_dlg.hold_ends.desc: "House change" means the next schedule block or anyone changing the house temperature, mode or preset — whichever comes first.
room_dlg.name: Name
room_dlg.offset.desc: e.g. −1 keeps a bedroom a degree cooler than the house. 0 = same as the house.
room_dlg.own_temps.desc: Comfort during the house's schedule blocks, Eco between them. Nook still decides when this room needs the boiler.
room_dlg.sensor.desc: Optional — otherwise the TRV's own reading is used.
room_dlg.sub_add: Pick the room's TRV — sensors are optional.
room_dlg.sub_edit: Change the TRV, sensors or boiler behaviour.
room_dlg.trv_config.desc: The TRV's own settings, as its integration (ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT, Z-Wave…) offers them. A change is sent to the TRV straight away.
room_dlg.trv_config.none: This TRV has no settings Home Assistant can change.
room_dlg.trv_config.pick: Pick a TRV above to see its settings.
room_dlg.trv_config.unavailable: TRV offline — can't change this now.
rooms.card.calls_boiler.tip: Let this room turn the boiler on
rooms.card.tip: Click to edit · drag to reorder
rooms.empty: No rooms yet — add your first one.
rooms.sub: Each room has its own Nook climate, driven by its TRV.
rooms.sub_edit: Click a room to edit it, drag to reorder.
rooms.title: Rooms
schedule.add_hint: Set the new block's day, times and temperature, then press Add
schedule.editing: Editing {day} {start}–{end}{overnight} — changes apply as you make them. Click an empty part of a row for a new block.
schedule.help: Orange dots are where blocks start. Outside blocks, Eco ({eco}°) applies and rooms drop to their own Eco temp. A block that starts inside another takes over until it ends; one that ends before it starts runs past midnight. Dial changes hold until the next block change.
schedule.new_block: New block — pick its day, times and temperature, then press Add. Click an orange dot to edit that block.
schedule.overlap: {day}: {later} starts during {earlier} — it takes over until it ends.
schedule.select_to_remove: Select an orange setpoint to remove
schedule.title: Schedule
seasonal.kept.one: {count} eased off because you turned it up
seasonal.kept.other: {count} eased off because you turned them up
seasonal.stop.tip: Stop and put the schedule temperatures back
seasonal.title: Winter Seasonal Savings
sensor_banner.backup: {main} isn't reporting — Nook is using {backup}{adjusted}. Check its battery.
sensor_banner.backup_since: {main} hasn't reported since {time} — Nook is using {backup}{adjusted}. Check its battery.
sensor_banner.none: No house sensor is reporting — Nook is heating on a timer (20 min each hour during schedule times, plus frost-protection runs). Check the sensor's battery.
sensor_banner.none_since: No house sensor has reported since {time} — Nook is heating on a timer (20 min each hour during schedule times, plus frost-protection runs). Check the sensor's battery.
sensors.empty: No temperature sensors yet — pick a house sensor above, or give a room its own sensor.
sensors.no_floor.desc: Put this sensor (or its device) in an area with a floor in Home Assistant's Areas & zones.
sensors.stuck: Reading hasn't changed since {time} while other sensors have — if the room has changed, try Reconfigure on this device in ZHA.
sensors.sub: Every sensor Nook reads. Faster updates asks a Zigbee (ZHA) sensor to report every 0.1°C or 5 min instead of 0.5°C or 15 min — Nook reacts sooner and overshoots less, for a little more battery.
sensors.title: Temperature Sensors
sensors.watch_add.desc: Add sensors from rooms Nook doesn't heat on (e.g. upstairs without TRVs). Nook shows them with their floor, and will learn from them — they don't turn the boiler on. Floors come from Home Assistant's Areas & zones.
settings.auto_schedule.desc: Adds or adjusts a schedule block when you make the same change at the same time on the same weekday, on two or more different days.
settings.away_delay.desc: How long everyone must be gone before Away (Eco) starts.
settings.backup_sensor.desc: Optional — used if the house sensor stops reporting (e.g. a flat battery). Nook learns how far apart the two usually read and adjusts for it.
settings.boiler.sub: Fine-tuning. The defaults suit most homes.
settings.boiler.title: Boiler Behaviour
settings.cold_preheat.desc: Lets True Radiant start warming up to 4 hours before a schedule block (normally 2) when the house is slow to heat, so it's still warm on time. Cheaper than keeping the house warmer overnight.
settings.cold_tol.desc: Heat starts this far below the target.
settings.devices.sub: The relay Nook switches and the sensors it heats to.
settings.devices.title: Heating Devices
settings.energy_sensor.desc: Optional — the boiler's or the gas supply's meter, in kWh or m³ (e.g. a smart meter's gas import). The wall panel's usage page shows what the heating used.
settings.heater.desc: Changing it turns the old relay off first.
settings.hot_tol.desc: Heat stops this far above the target.
settings.house_sensor.desc: The temperature Nook heats the house to.
settings.intel.sub: Learning and comfort features for the house.
settings.leaf.desc: Shows the leaf when you're saving energy.
settings.min_off.desc: Shortest rest between runs (1–30 min). 3–5 min suits most boilers.
settings.min_on.desc: Shortest boiler run (1–30 min). 3–5 min suits most boilers.
settings.need_devices: Pick a boiler relay and a house temperature sensor
settings.outdoor_sensor.desc: Optional — lets preheat learn how cold weather slows warming up.
settings.pin.desc: Unlocks wall panels that have Temperature lock on. It's also the PIN for Fully's menu on panels Nook manages; leave it blank to keep Fully's own PIN.
settings.presence.empty: Nobody added yet — Away mode is off until you add someone.
settings.presence.sub: Who lives here. Nook switches to Away once everyone has left.
settings.presence.title: Presence
settings.safety.enabled.desc: Forces heat even in Away, Eco or Off if the house gets this cold.
settings.safety.title: Safety Temperature
settings.seasonal.desc: For 3 weeks, lowers each schedule block 0.1°C every 3 days (up to 0.5°C). Turn the heat up during a block and that block eases off and is left alone. At the end the new temperatures are saved into your schedule. Needs the schedule on.
settings.stale.desc: No report for this long means a flat battery or lost signal. Zigbee sensors check in at least every 15 min (5 min with faster updates).
settings.summer.desc: Never calls for heat (the safety floor still applies).
settings.temps.title: Temperatures & Modes
settings.title: Settings
settings.true_radiant.desc: Starts heating early so it's warm when a schedule block begins, and stops early by the learned radiator coast.
settings.warmup.coast_learned.one: Radiators coast {coast} °C after the boiler stops ({count} run).
settings.warmup.coast_learned.other: Radiators coast {coast} °C after the boiler stops ({count} runs).
settings.warmup.default: Using the default {rate} °C/h until it has learned from a few heat runs.
settings.warmup.desc: Times preheating and when to stop. Reset if they were learned while the heating was faulty.
settings.warmup.reset_confirm: Forget the learned warm-up rate and radiator coast? Nook goes back to its defaults and learns again from the next heat runs.
settings.windows.add: Add a window or door sensor
settings.windows.pause_after.desc: How long a window or door must stay open first, so walking through a door doesn't stop the heating. Rooms' own sensors use it too. 0 = straight away.
settings.windows.sub: When one of these stays open, the house stops calling for heat until it's shut.
settings.windows.title: Windows & Doors
wall.card.kiosk_mode.off_hint: Turn it on once at the panel: Fully Settings → Kiosk Mode → Enable Kiosk Mode (Fully won't allow it remotely).
wall.lead: Each wall screen or tablet. On the device, you only pick which panel it is.
wall.reported.mismatch.tip: Only the preview uses this; the panel already lays itself out to fit
wall.reported.waiting: Shows once the panel has opened Nook
wall.title: Wall Panels
wall_dlg.clock_after.desc: Idle time before the Nook app shows its clock. A tap (or a wave close to the screen) clears it; the screen turns off later — see "Screen off after" in the kiosk settings.
wall_dlg.delete_confirm: Delete wall panel “{name}”? The device will need setting up again.
wall_dlg.device_id.auto: Filled in from the name. You'll choose this on the panel.
wall_dlg.device_id.fixed: Fixed — the panel uses it to find its settings.
wall_dlg.host_looks_like_code: Panel IP address looks like a code — enter an address like 192.168.1.50, or leave it blank
wall_dlg.id_exists: A panel with ID “{id}” already exists
wall_dlg.kiosk.device.desc: Linking lets Nook set this panel's start URL and settings for you.
wall_dlg.kiosk.no_integration: Add the Fully Kiosk Browser integration in Home Assistant (needs Fully's Plus licence) and Nook can set this panel's start page and settings for you.
wall_dlg.kiosk.overrides: Settings here apply to this panel only and override the house settings Nook keeps for every panel (Kiosk Browser card on the Wall panels page). Leave a setting on “House: …” or “Not managed” to follow the house setting.
wall_dlg.kiosk_enabled.desc: Turn off for screens that can't run it (no app installs) — Nook then leaves this panel's browser alone.
wall_dlg.lock.no_pin: Needs a Wall panel PIN in Settings first.
wall_dlg.lock.on: Changes on the panel need the house PIN.
wall_dlg.name: Name
wall_dlg.shape.desc: Sizes the preview. The panel fits itself to its real screen, and turns with a tablet.
wall_dlg.shows.desc: Blank sensors use the house ones from Settings. Room buttons always follow your Rooms list.
wall_dlg.sub_add: Set up a new wall screen or tablet. You'll pick this panel on the device.
wall_dlg.sub_edit: Change what this panel shows and controls.
wall_dlg.thermostat.nook: Nook's house thermostat — schedule, presets and boiler control all apply.
wall_dlg.thermostat.not_nook: This isn't a Nook thermostat, so the panel will bypass Nook's schedule and boiler control.
